# Frame

The Page runs the full height, and meets a docked Sidebar at its 1px edge. - The Frame owns the Sidebar state and hands it to the Sidebar through `SidebarControlContext`. Open, the toggle (`angles-left`) ends the Sidebar's logo row; closed, the Frame draws it (`bars`) at the Page's top left, centered on x 32, and the Page's header row (`header`, the breadcrumb) follows it on the same center line from x 56. - What docks is decided by the layout resolver (`./frameLayout`) from the Frame's own width: from 1024 the Sidebar docks (240, in flow); under 1024 it never docks. - Docked, the Sidebar sits on the sunken fill with a 1px `--ds-border` on its Page-facing edge. Floating (a peek, or opened by hand under 1024) it lies over the Page on `--ds-surface-material-overlay` with `--ds-shadow-overlay` and no Blanket. - Hovering the left edge peeks a closed Sidebar. An outside press, Escape, or the pointer leaving closes the peek. Floating, the Sidebar is a non-modal Base UI `Dialog`: its dismissal and its focus return run there, and Escape hands focus to the toggle that is left. - Either toggle, or Ctrl+[ (Cmd+[ on a Mac), closes a showing Sidebar and opens a closed one; focus follows to the toggle that is left. - Opening a modal closes a floating Sidebar and leaves a docked one alone, and while one is open the Sidebar does not peek. The frame hears it from the shared overlay module (`@/lib/overlay`), so a page does not wire its modals to the frame. A modal opened from inside the floating Sidebar hands focus to the toggle when it closes, since its trigger left with the Sidebar. - The Panel area (`panel`) is the Frame's right-hand area. A Details Panel (`panelKind="details"`, the default) always floats as an overlay at every width with no Blanket, so the Page and Sidebar keep their full width. Only the AI chat panel (`panelKind="ai"`) docks beside the Page at a hairline when the content keeps 720, collapsing a default Sidebar first (and restoring it when the Panel closes). As an overlay, either Panel floats over the Page on the overlay material and shadow, with no Blanket, and a press outside or Escape closes it (a press on a trigger with `aria-controls` leaves it open to swap or toggle). Under 1024 it is capped at 320, and only one overlay is open at a time; under 768 it is full width. From 768 up a floating Details Panel is not modal so the Page and Sidebar stay usable; focus moves into an overlay Panel when it opens and returns to the opener when it closes. An overlay AI panel (and a full-width Details Panel under 768) is modal with the Page and Sidebar inert. Docked or peeking it is not modal and leaves focus where it is. Its open state, dismissal and focus run on Base UI's `Dialog`, portaled into the Frame's row so a dock or overlay switch never remounts the Panel's content. Its splitter resizes it from 320 to 640 (when docked, never past what keeps 720 beside a docked Sidebar) by drag or keys. Width and open state are kept in sessionStorage. A modal leaves it open. Anything inside the Frame opens it through `usePanelControl`. - A multi-step task runs in the Sidebar's inner mode: its steps are the rows, and the Page's footer holds the task's actions. - Landmarks: the Page is `main`; the Sidebar's `nav` is the navigation; the Panel is a complementary landmark named by `panelLabel`. - The Page pads `--page-pad` (24 at every width) and caps its content at `--content-max-width` (1232), centered (`width="full"` lifts the cap, `width="reading"` caps it at 864), on a 12-column grid with a 16 gutter. Children span all 12 columns unless they set `grid-column`.

Every full page starts in the app frame: the Sidebar beside the Page, with the AI panel as its own region. Two types: default and bare. A multi-step task runs in the Sidebar's inner mode.

Also asked as: page template, page shell, page layout, full page, new page, surface container.

## Usage

Use Frame for every page of the app. It owns the frame sizes and the Sidebar's behavior, so a page only supplies its Sidebar, its breadcrumb and its content.

The Frame decides what docks from its own width, not the window's, through one layout resolver, so the content never drops under 720:

- **Sidebar.** Below its docking width, opened by hand, it floats over the Page and closes on an outside press or Escape. Hovering the toggle or the left edge peeks a collapsed Sidebar over the Page with no Blanket. Clicking the toggle, or pressing Ctrl+[, closes a docked Sidebar and opens a collapsed one.
- **AI panel and Details Panel.** The Panel area opens from anything inside the Frame through `usePanelControl()`. Only the AI panel (`panelKind="ai"`) docks: both dock when the Sidebar, the panel and the content minimum fit, otherwise a Sidebar left open by default collapses and comes back when the panel closes, and below that the AI panel floats on the overlay fill and shadow with no Blanket. A Details Panel (`panelKind="details"`, the default) always floats over the Page on the overlay fill and shadow at every width, with no Blanket, while the Page and Sidebar keep their full width. From 768 up a floating Details Panel stays non-modal so the Page and Sidebar remain usable.
- **Page width.** Everything inside the Frame, overlays included, reads the page's width through `usePageNarrow()` from `@/lib/pageWidth`: true under 768, false outside a Frame. Tabs takes its narrow form from it.
- **Narrow Frames** hold one layer open at a time: opening the Sidebar closes the panel, and opening the panel closes the Sidebar.
- **Modals.** Opening a Modal closes a peeking or floating Sidebar, and a docked Sidebar stays. While a Modal is open the Sidebar does not peek, and Escape closes the Modal only. A Modal leaves the panel open under its Blanket.

Docked, the panel meets the Page at a hairline. Its splitter resizes it from 320 to 640, but never past what keeps 720 beside a docked Sidebar. The width and whether the panel is open are kept for the tab.

## Motion

Frame reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sidebar-open | Dock and undock a panel | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | The Sidebar opens on spatial.default while the Page narrows on the same clock. The Sidebar never moves when the Page changes. |
| sidebar-close | Dock and undock a panel | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | It closes on spatial.fast to its edge and leaves nothing behind: no rail. |
| panel-dock | Dock and undock a panel | `--ds-motion-spatial-slow` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The AI Panel docks on the right and the Page makes room; its content fades in once the page is about 90% done. |
| panel-undock | Dock and undock a panel | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | It reverses and stays at the edge. |
| step | Step to the next or previous | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The body slides on the same axis as the step list: up with the steps down the left, across with four or fewer across the top. Step states change in place. Placement is set once, when the task opens, by the longest path the flow can take. |

## Alternatives

- For a bare fill and elevation, use `Page`.
- For a region inside the content, use `Section`.
- For a short task that keeps the page in view behind it, use `Modal`. A multi-step task runs in the Sidebar's inner mode.

## Best practices

### Give a multi-step task its steps in the inner sidebar. {#give-a-multi-step-task-its-steps-in-the-inner-sidebar}

**Checked:** Review

The steps are the Sidebar's rows, so the Page holds only the task. Done steps tick and stay pressable; steps past your answers are off. The page places the footer along the bottom today; the Frame's `bar` slot is Planned.

Do: The steps as rows in the inner sidebar; the Page holds only the task.
Don't: The steps drawn again inside the Page: two lists for one task.

### Put Save and exit, Back and Next in the footer, with no Cancel. {#put-save-and-exit-back-and-next-in-the-footer-with-no-cancel}

**Checked:** Review

The footer is fixed along the bottom, one row high, with its buttons on one line. Save and exit leaves the task and keeps the answers, so the footer holds only it, Back and the primary Next. Back on the first step is disabled and needs no reason.

Do: Save and exit as a link at the left edge; Back and the primary Next in the right half, on one line.
Don't: Cancel repeated in the footer beside Save and exit: two ways out of one task.

### Dock the AI panel where there is room, and float it beside narrow layouts. {#dock-the-ai-panel-where-there-is-room-and-float-it-beside-narrow-layouts}

**Checked:** Review

Only the AI panel (`panelKind="ai"`) docks as a region of the Frame, so it stays put as a person moves between pages (Details Panels always float over the Page with no Blanket). The Page makes room for the AI panel while the Frame is wide enough to keep the Page above its floor. Where the Frame is not, the AI panel floats over the Page and the Sidebar, with no Blanket. The widths are under Width behavior.

### Keep a bare Frame to one column. {#keep-a-bare-frame-to-one-column}

**Checked:** Review

Sign-in, errors and welcome have one job and no account yet, so the Frame carries no Sidebar, header row or Panel.

Do: One centered column: the form and its button.
Don't: The Sidebar beside a sign-in: navigation for a person who has not signed in.

### Put the place in the header as a breadcrumb. {#put-the-place-in-the-header-as-a-breadcrumb}

**Checked:** Review

The header row is the breadcrumb, shown only after drilling into a record; area pages and multi-step tasks have none. A page's title is the PageHeader at the top of the Page, its one h1; a Section never stands in for it.

Elevation and fills follow Elevation.

## Accessibility

- The Page is the `main` landmark, and the `nav` inside the Sidebar is the navigation landmark. Pass `contentAs="div"` when the page supplies its own `main`.
- The toggle is a button. Open, it ends the Sidebar's logo row as "Close sidebar"; closed, it sits at the Page's top left as "Open sidebar". It reports whether the Sidebar is showing and announces its shortcut, Ctrl+[ (Cmd+[ on a Mac).
- A peeking or floating Sidebar closes on Escape, and focus returns to the toggle.
- Docked, the AI panel is a complementary landmark named by `panelLabel`, after the Page in reading order. Below `FRAME_LAYOUT.dockMin` it is a Modal-style layer: focus moves to its first control, Tab stays inside it, the Page and the Sidebar under it are inert, and closing returns focus to what opened it.
- The splitter is a vertical separator named "Resize panel" that reports its width. The left arrow widens the panel by 16 and the right arrow narrows it, 64 with Shift; Home and End go to the narrowest and the widest.
- A multi-step task's steps are a list named "Steps" in the Sidebar's navigation; the current step is marked, a done step is named "Done", and an off step is not pressable. The footer's buttons follow the body in the tab order.

## Related

- Page: use when you need the bare fill-and-elevation the content box is built on.
- Sidebar: use when choosing what the Frame places beside the Page.
- Section: use when the content needs a region under its own heading.
- Modal: use when the task is short and the page should stay in view behind it.
- Panel: use when the work should float beside the page, not replace it.
- Grid: use when you need the column math the Frame is sized by.

Same group: `Card` · `Modal` · `Page` · `Panel` · `Section` · `Table`

## Types

Choose one of two Frame types for every app page, shown here in browser windows. Browser chrome frames full pages only: a Frame-rooted screen draws in a browser window, and a Section, Card, Table or any other block draws bare. See Templates and patterns for how filled Frames become Screens and Flows, documented with the flows.

- **Default.** Pages people move among: the Sidebar, the Page, and the AI panel as its own region on the right.
- **Bare.** Sign-in, errors and welcome: one centered column, with no Sidebar and no header row.

## Anatomy

### Default

The default type at 1440 with the AI panel docked.

1. **Sidebar.** 240 wide, docked from 1024, with the toggle ending its logo row.
2. **Header row.** The Page's first row, 32 high on the logo row's center line: the breadcrumb, once a person has drilled into a record.
3. **Content.** The Page's content box: no corner radius, a 24 pad, and a 12-column grid capped at 1232 (864 at reading width, no cap at full width).
4. **Panel area.** A Frame region on the right, 320 to 640 and opening at 400, with its splitter on the left hairline. Only the AI panel (`panelKind="ai"`) docks — from 1168 with a 400 panel, from 1408 beside an open Sidebar, floating over the Page under that; a Details Panel (`panelKind="details"`, the default) always floats over the Page with no Blanket.

## Width behavior

The Frame decides what docks from its own width, so the content never drops under 720. Only the AI panel (`panelKind="ai"`) docks; Details Panels (`panelKind="details"`, the default) always float over the Page at every width with no Blanket. Drag the width: the Sidebar and an open AI panel both dock from 1408 with a 400 panel; from 1168 the AI panel docks alone and the Sidebar collapses; below that, and under 1024, it floats over the Page with no Blanket. Under 768 any panel is full width. The Sidebar docks from 1024 (in Figma, the `Sidebar docked` variable); in code the Frame measures its own width through the layout resolver and has no token for it.

## Key states

- **AI panel collapses the Sidebar, 1200.** The Sidebar, a 400 AI panel and 720 of content cannot all fit, so the Sidebar collapses and the toggle moves to the Page's top left. It comes back when the panel closes.

- **Under 1024.** The Sidebar never docks: opened by hand it floats over the Page. The panel floats over the Page with no Blanket, and one layer is open at a time.

A system banner, when one is needed, spans the whole width above the Sidebar and the Page: Notifications.

## Slots

| Slot or prop | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `sidebar` | The Sidebar. Without it there is no Sidebar and no toggle. |
| `header` | The Page's header row: the breadcrumb. |
| `children` | The content: Sections in a 12-column grid. `width` sets the Page type: `default` caps it at 1232, `full` has no cap, `reading` caps it at 864. |
| `panel` · `panelKind` · `panelLabel` · `panelOpen` | The Panel area at the right, named for its content, filled with the Panel parts. `panelKind` is `'details'` (default, always floats over the Page with no Blanket) or `'ai'` (opts in to dock where there is room). |
| `surfaceDirect` | Children go straight into the Page with no content box, for a bare column or a full-bleed view. |
| `bar` | Planned. The multi-step footer, 52 high with 32-high buttons holding Save and exit, Back and Next. Today the page places the footer. |
| `banner` | Planned. System news across the whole width above the Sidebar and the Page. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the multi-step task for what it does: "Plan a tutoring term". | A generic title such as "Wizard". |
| Name the panel for its content with `panelLabel`: "AI chat". | A generic name such as "Panel". |
| Name steps with one noun each: "Student", "Schedule", "Review". | A sentence for a step. |
| Keep Back and Next named for what they do. | Icon buttons with no name. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `areaKey` | string or number | — | Current Sidebar area key: changing it fades the old page out on `appearance.fast`, then fades the new page in on `appearance.default`. |
| `header` | node | — | The Page's header row, 32 high on the logo row's center line: the breadcrumb. While the Sidebar is closed it follows the toggle. |
| `sidebar` | node | — | Sidebar content. Without it there is no Sidebar and no toggle. |
| `sidebarDocked` | bool | — | Sets the Sidebar's default request: true opens it, false closes it. Under 1024 it never docks. Unset opens it where it fits. |
| `panel` | node | — | Panel area content, usually a `PanelContainer` and its parts. Without it there is no Panel. |
| `panelKind` | enum | `'details'` | Whether the Panel is a Details Panel (`'details'`, the default — always floats over the Page with no Blanket) or the dockable AI panel (`'ai'`). |
| `panelLabel` | string | `'AI chat'` | The Panel's complementary landmark name, named for its content. |
| `panelOpen` | bool | — | Controlled open state. Leave unset to let the Frame keep it (and remember it for the tab). |
| `defaultPanelOpen` | bool | `false` | Uncontrolled: whether the Panel starts open when the tab has nothing remembered. |
| `onPanelOpenChange` | func | — | Called with the next open state whenever the Panel opens or closes. |
| `panelDefaultWidth` | number | `FRAME_LAYOUT.panelDefault` | The width (px) the Panel opens at when the tab has nothing remembered: 320 to 640, default 400. |
| `panelPeek` | bool | `false` | Hovering the Frame's right edge peeks a closed Panel over the Page, with no Blanket. Off by default. |
| `panelStorageKey` | string | `PANEL_STORAGE_KEY` | The sessionStorage key the Panel's width and open state are kept under; null keeps nothing. |
| `width` | enum | `'default'` | Content type: default caps the grid at 1232, full has no cap (chat, a board, a wide table), reading caps it at 864. |
| `contentAs` | elementType | — | Element for the content box. `main` by default, the Page's landmark; pass `div` when the page supplies its own `main`. |
| `contentClassName` | string | `''` | — |
| `surfaceDirect` | bool | `false` | Render children straight into the page, with no content box or grid (full-bleed views). The Page itself is then the `main`. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |
| `children` | node | — | Content slot |
